script: Here is the best NBA player at every height heading into the 2026 season. At 5'7", we have Yuki Kawamura, the shortest player currently listed in the NBA. Last year, he was listed at 5'8", but this year, he was listed at 5'7". Next, at 5'11", we have Naji Nimhard, not to be confused with his brother Andrew Nembhard, who's 6'4". At 6'0", Fred VanVleet. 6'1", Darius Garland. At 6'2", Jalen Brunson or Stephen Curry. Steph is easiest, but you tell me: would you rather have a 38-year-old Steph Curry next season or a 30-year-old Jalen Brunson heading into next season? 6'3" Donovan Mitchell. 6'4" Anthony Edwards. 6'5" Tyrese Haliburton. Assuming he comes back in full health. 6'6" Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. 6'7" Kawhi Leonard. Still going with Kawhi Leonard. The question is, is he playing for the Raptors, Clippers, or will he be suspended for the season? 6'8" Luka Doncic. 6'9" LeBron James. 6'10" Anthony Davis. 6'11" Nikola Jokic or Giannis Antetokounmpo. I don't want to get into that debate. 7' Karl-Anthony Towns. 7'1" Rudy Gobert. 7'2" Kristaps Porzingis. 7'3" Zach Edey. 7'4" Victor Wembanyama. Last year, he was listed at 7'5", but this year, he is listed at 7'4". 7'5" Keyonte George. Second-tallest active NBA player. And 7'6" Taco Fall.
